purpose: Local MLBB gameplay and draft screenshots for UI state classification, minimap calibration, scoreboard extraction, item-shop recognition, and live coaching signal design.

coverage: lane/role icons on left player rail
useFor: role icon detection on player rail

minimap.notes: Live HUD samples show minimap markers, pings, objective circles, hero portraits, lane dots, turret icons, and death overlay dimming. The minimap remains visible under most live/death overlays and is suitable for marker segmentation.

topHud.notes: Contains team score, game clock, alive/death timers, and kill feed portraits. Needs separate masks for draft screens because the top bar has a different layout there.

scoreboardBody.notes: Equipment and attributes layouts share the same modal frame but require separate extractors. Equipment has sparse icon columns; attributes has dense numeric columns.

draftCenterGrid.notes: Hero grid and 3D model states occupy the same broad center area. Classifier should first separate grid vs model/confirmation views before hero recognition.

draftLeftRail.notes: Stable source for allied player slots, lane icons, requested heroes, and selected heroes during draft.

draftRightRail.notes: Stable source for enemy slots and selected heroes. Empty-slot placeholders are strong cues for pick phase progress.

shopPanel.notes: Large modal with tabs, recommended items, build path, and purchase button. It should be excluded from live HUD/minimap coaching except for item recommendation features.

implementationFindings: The current capture regions cover minimap and scoreboard/window activation, but they do not yet distinguish draft, loading, shop, death replay, or live HUD states.
A lightweight screen-state classifier should run before deeper OCR/recognition so the app does not try to parse draft screens as live gameplay.
Scoreboard extraction needs two modes: equipment/build icons and attributes/numeric stats.
The draft samples are rich enough to add first-pass state labels for ban phase, ally pick, enemy pick, and match-start preparation.
The live samples show that death replay and kill banners dim the screen, so minimap detection should use marker color/shape rather than global brightness alone.
